    The display-ready shape of a descriptive table

    Source: R/describe.R
    sdt_describe_render.Rd

    Renders a sdt_describe() object as a flat table of character columns, one row per level or statistic, ready for knitr::kable(), DT or any other table renderer. The numbers are formatted with the object's digits; the object itself keeps them unrounded.

    Usage

    sdt_describe_render(x)

    Arguments

    x

    A sdt_describe object.

    Value

    A tibble::tibble() of character columns with a footnotes attribute.

    Details

    Missingness follows the object's na_report: a (missing) row, a pair of missing columns, or a footnote. The legend naming each percent's denominator is always the first footnote, so a rendered table can never arrive without one.

    See also

    sdt_describe().

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(grade = c("consultant", "resident", NA), years = c(9, 3, 5))
sdt_describe_render(sdt_describe(d))
#> # A tibble: 7 × 7
#>   variable what         value             n     imputed `val%` `all%`
#> * <chr>    <chr>        <chr>             <chr> <chr>   <chr>  <chr> 
#> 1 grade    consultant   1 (50.0%)         "1"   "0"     "50.0" "33.3"
#> 2 grade    resident     1 (50.0%)         "1"   "0"     "50.0" "33.3"
#> 3 grade    (missing)    1 (33.3%)         "1"   "-"     "-"    "33.3"
#> 4 years    mean (SD)    5.67 (3.06)       "3"   "0"     ""     ""    
#> 5 years    median [IQR] 5.00 [4.00, 7.00] ""    ""      ""     ""    
#> 6 years    range        3.00 to 9.00      ""    ""      ""     ""    
#> 7 years    (missing)    0 (0.0%)          ""    ""      ""     ""
